corpus_definition: A person's name written in their own way as proof.

forms.definition: your name written in your own special way, for example on a document
forms.example: Please add your signature at the bottom of the form.

syn.note: An autograph is a famous person's signature that they give to a fan.
General word; a signature is your name written by your own hand.

forms.definition: to write your name on a paper to show you wrote it or agree with it
forms.example: You need to sign the contract before you start work.
forms.note: The g is silent in sign but you hear it in signature.

syn.note: Used when a famous person writes their name for a fan: 'He autographed my ball.'
To write only the first letters of your name, often on each page.
Formal: to write your name on the back of a cheque.

forms.definition: having someone's name written on it by that person
forms.example: I have a signed copy of her new book.

syn.note: Used for books, photos or shirts with a famous person's name on them.

ant.note: Without a name written on it: an unsigned letter.

people.definition: a person or country that has put their name on an official agreement
people.example: Uzbekistan is a signatory to the international agreement.

context.text: At the bank, I had to sign three papers before they gave me my new card. The worker checked that my signature looked the same as the one in my passport.

reviewer_note: Two corpus rows with the same meaning merged into one map. Family is built from the verb sign; no affix from the table applies (-ure, -ed, -ory are not in the list).

corpus_definition: A state where there is no sound.

forms.definition: a time or place when there is no sound at all
forms.example: There was complete silence in the room.

syn.note: Easy word; quiet can mean only a little sound, not none.
No sound and no movement; often used about nature.
A short, calm quiet, often after noise stops.

ant.note: Noise is sound, especially loud or unpleasant sound.
Sound is anything you can hear.

forms.definition: to make someone or something stop making a sound or speaking
forms.example: The teacher silenced the class with one look.

syn.note: British English; American English usually says 'quiet'.
Often used about calming children or a crowd.
Informal and often rude: to make someone stop talking.

forms.definition: with no sound, or not speaking at all
forms.example: The streets of Khiva were silent at night.

syn.note: Easy word; quiet means little sound, silent means none.
Very close, more literary.
Very close; often about machines that make no noise.

ant.note: Making a strong sound that is easy to hear.

forms.definition: without making any sound at all
forms.example: The cat moved across the floor silently.

syn.note: Easy word; quietly can mean with a little sound.
Very close, less common.
Very close, more literary.

ant.note: In a way that makes a lot of sound.
In a strong voice or with strong sound.

people.definition: a device fixed to a gun or engine to make it much quieter
people.example: The mechanic put a new silencer on my car.
people.note: In American English the car part is called a muffler.

context.text: When the teacher came in, there was silence in the classroom. Everyone sat silent at their desks and silently opened their books.

reviewer_note: silence is both noun and verb (conversion); silencer is a thing noun, so it goes in People & things.

corpus_definition: Without making any noise at all.

forms.definition: a time or place when there is no sound at all
forms.example: We walked through the forest in silence.

syn.note: Easy word; quiet can mean only a little sound, not none.
No sound and no movement; often used about nature.

ant.note: Noise is sound, especially loud or unpleasant sound.

forms.definition: to make someone or something stop making a sound or speaking
forms.example: She silenced her phone before the meeting.

syn.note: British English; American English usually says 'quiet'.
Often used about calming children or a crowd.

forms.definition: with no sound, or not speaking at all
forms.example: The baby was finally silent and asleep.

syn.note: Easy word; quiet means little sound, silent means none.
Very close, more literary.
Very close; often about machines that make no noise.

ant.note: Making a strong sound that is easy to hear.

forms.definition: without making any sound at all
forms.example: The cat moved across the floor silently.

syn.note: Easy word; quietly can mean with a little sound.
Very close, less common.
Very close, more literary.

ant.note: In a way that makes a lot of sound.
In a strong voice or with strong sound.

people.definition: a device fixed to a gun or engine to make it much quieter
people.example: The old car needed a new silencer.
people.note: In American English the car part is called a muffler.

context.text: My grandmother prays silently every morning. The house is silent, and nobody breaks the silence until she finishes.

reviewer_note: Headword is the adverb; same family as the silence map, anchored on the adverb.

corpus_definition: An action that breaks a religious or moral rule.

forms.definition: a bad action that breaks a religious or moral rule
forms.example: Many people believe lying is a serious sin.

syn.note: Bad or illegal actions in general; not always religious.
Evil is very bad or cruel behaviour; stronger and more general.
A crime breaks the law of a country; a sin breaks a religious or moral rule.

ant.note: A virtue is a good quality or good way of behaving.

forms.definition: to break a religious or moral rule
forms.example: He believed he had sinned and asked God to forgive him.

syn.note: Easy phrase; not always about religion.
Very formal and rare in speech.

forms.definition: morally wrong, or breaking a religious rule
forms.example: Some people think it is sinful to waste bread.
forms.note: Also used jokingly about food that is very nice but unhealthy: a sinful chocolate cake.

syn.note: Very bad and wrong; a little old-fashioned.
Against what people think is right; not always religious.
Easy, general word for bad behaviour.

ant.note: Behaving in a very good and moral way.

forms.definition: in a way that is morally wrong or breaks a religious rule
forms.example: He felt he had lived sinfully when he was young.

syn.note: In a very bad way; a little old-fashioned.
In a way that is against what is right.

ant.note: In a very good and moral way.

people.definition: a person who has broken a religious or moral rule
people.example: The imam said that every sinner can ask for forgiveness.

context.text: My grandmother says that wasting bread is a sin. She thinks it is sinful to throw food away when other people are hungry.

reviewer_note: Kept the religious/moral sense only; sin as the maths abbreviation (sine) is unrelated and left out.

corpus_definition: the bone structure that forms and protects the head

forms.definition: the bones of the head that protect the brain
forms.example: The doctor looked at an X-ray of his skull after the accident.

syn.note: The medical word; doctors and scientists use it.
The whole top part of the body; the skull is only the bone inside.
General word; the skull is a group of bones.

context.text: My little brother fell off his bike, so we took him to the hospital. Luckily, the X-ray showed that his skull was not broken.

reviewer_note: Single-form family. Compounds (skullcap, which is the doppi) are left for the Compounds branch.

corpus_definition: Websites where people talk and share news with friends.
usage_note: Uncountable noun; can take a singular or plural verb: 'Social media is/are changing our lives.' Use 'on social media': 'I saw it on social media.' Also before nouns: a social media post, social media apps.

relations.note: One website or app of this kind, like Instagram or Telegram; social media means all of them together.
The whole computer network; social media is only one part of it.
TV, radio and newspapers that reach many people; ordinary people can post on social media.

context.text: My sister spends hours on social media every evening. She says she gets most of her news from social media, not from TV.

reviewer_note: Fixed noun phrase; no true antonym listed.

corpus_definition: Power that we get directly from the light of the sun.
usage_note: Uncountable: say 'solar energy', not 'a solar energy'. Common verbs: use, produce, generate solar energy. Solar = of the sun: solar panels, the solar system.

relations.note: Almost the same; solar power is more common when we talk about electricity.
Energy that never runs out, like sun, wind and water; solar energy is one type.
Solar energy is often turned into electricity.

context.text: Uzbekistan has more than 300 sunny days a year, so solar energy is a good choice. Many new houses near Tashkent now use solar energy for hot water.

reviewer_note: Fixed noun phrase; no true antonym (fossil fuels contrast, but are not an opposite).

forms.definition: a way to end a problem or a difficult situation
forms.example: He found a solution to the error in the program.

syn.note: Easy, everyday word with the same meaning.
Informal; often a quick answer to a technical problem.
Something that makes a bad situation better; also a medicine.
A way to escape a difficult situation.

ant.note: The problem is the difficulty; the solution ends it.

forms.definition: to find the answer to a problem or question
forms.example: Dilnoza solved the maths problem in two minutes.

syn.note: Common phrasal verb, especially for sums and puzzles.
More formal; often about disagreements.
Informal: fix a problem or a mess.
Easy word; usually about repairing something broken.

forms.definition: possible to find an answer to
forms.example: Don't worry, this problem is solvable.

syn.note: Very close and more formal.

ant.note: Impossible to find an answer to.
Formal: an insoluble problem has no answer.

forms.definition: able to mix completely into a liquid
forms.example: Sugar is soluble in water.
forms.note: Belongs to solution = a liquid with something mixed into it, not the answer to a problem.

people.definition: a person who finds answers to problems or puzzles
people.example: Aziz is a great problem solver at work.

context.text: Our teacher gave us a very hard puzzle. Dilnoza was the first to solve it, and she explained her solution to the whole class.

reviewer_note: Sense trap: solution = answer vs solution = liquid mixture; soluble belongs to the liquid sense and is marked other_meaning.

corpus_definition: To fix a problem or organize things.
particle_note: Separable: 'sort out the problem' or 'sort the problem out'. With a pronoun the particle goes after it: 'sort it out'. Mostly British English and informal.

relations.note: More neutral; sort out is more informal and can also mean organize.
Easy word for making a problem go away.
To take action to solve a problem.
Used for the 'put things in order' meaning. British spelling: organise.
To make a room or place neat.
Informal: to spoil something or make it untidy.

context.text: My room was a mess, so I spent Saturday sorting out my clothes and books. Then I helped my dad sort out a problem with his phone.

reviewer_note: Corpus definition covers both 'fix a problem' and 'organize'; one map, both shown in the context.

corpus_definition: Where something comes from or starts.

forms.definition: the place, person or thing that something comes from
forms.example: This river is the main source of our water.
forms.note: Also used for a person or book that gives information: a news source.

syn.note: Very close; origin is more about where something began long ago.
The first part or start of something.
The thing that makes something happen: the source of the problem.
The basic cause of a problem: the root of the trouble.

forms.definition: to get something, such as food or materials, from a particular place
forms.example: The restaurant sources its vegetables from local farms.
forms.note: Mostly used in business English, often in the passive: 'locally sourced meat'.

syn.note: Formal word for get.
Easy, general word; source says where it comes from.
To pay for something; sourcing is about choosing where to get it.

forms.note: No adjective in this family. Resource is a different word, not made from source.

context.text: The Amu Darya is an important source of water for farms in Karakalpakstan. Many shops in Nukus source their fruit from these farms.

reviewer_note: Noun and verb are the same spelling (conversion); the verb is business English. Resource listed as not_family.
